purpose: How RivetIT implements the controls RivetCore's security baseline leaves to the edition (status edition-responsibility, or partial and needing the edition). Statuses are conservative: 'enforced' only when a named test in this repository proves the behaviour. Checked by scripts/edition-baseline-check.php; the public Security and trust page renders its counts. Wording rules: vendor/rivet/rivet-core/docs/security/CLAIMS.md.

controls.how: Staff password minimum is the setting password_min_length, never below SecurityBaseline::MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH (12) even if an old row holds a lower number; passphrases of 64 characters and more are accepted (limit 1024); no composition rules; refused when equal to name, username or email.
controls.note: Default is 12 (baseline default 14 is a recommendation, not a floor).

controls.how: New hashes are Argon2id (64 MiB, 3 passes); old bcrypt hashes still verify and are rehashed at the next successful sign-in.
Optional Have I Been Pwned range check (k-anonymity, only the 5 character SHA-1 prefix leaves the server, through RivetCore's UrlPolicy). Off by default and fails open.
controls.note: Gap by default: an administrator has to switch it on.

controls.how: TOTP and passkeys with single-use recovery codes; policy off | admins | all with a grace period; remember-me cannot stand in for the second factor of an administrator.
controls.note: Gap against the baseline: the policy default is 'off', so administrators are not forced to enrol until an administrator sets the policy. SecurityBaseline::mfaRequired() is not wired in because forcing it would lock out installations that have not enrolled yet; a decision for the maintainer.

controls.how: Password reset tokens are single use and expire; there is no default account (the installer makes the operator choose the first administrator password, minimum 12 characters).
controls.note: The staff reset flow is covered by the password-policy test only; no dedicated test for token expiry and single use.

controls.how: The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure on HTTPS (strict mode on); the vault-key cookie is SameSite=Strict.
controls.note: Gap: the cookie name does not carry the __Host- prefix (SecurityBaseline::hostCookieName() is not used), because renaming PHPSESSID would sign every user out and the app can run on plain HTTP in development.

controls.how: Idle timeout (default 480 minutes) and absolute lifetime (default 14 days) are enforced server side; sessions are listed and revocable; a password change revokes every other session; the vault asks for the password again after 15 idle minutes.
controls.note: Deviates from the baseline: default 480 instead of 30 minutes, and an administrator may raise the idle timeout above the 480 minute ceiling (the setting accepts up to 90 days, used with remember-me). SecurityBaseline::effective('session_idle_minutes') is not applied.

controls.how: Every cookie-authenticated POST handler validates a CSRF token (validateCSRFToken); the API uses bearer tokens, not cookies.
controls.note: Verified by reading: 168 files call validateCSRFToken. The HTTP test needs the scratch web environment; it was not green in the 2026-10 parity run (environment, not code: same result without the parity changes).

controls.how: Administrative pages require an administrator role; the MFA gate applies when the MFA policy is on; nginx denies the non-public trees and metadata files (static test).
controls.note: Administrator MFA depends on AUTH-07 (policy default off).

controls.how: The RMM data store form refuses weak transport (disable/allow/prefer) to a remote host unless an explicit, audit-logged acknowledgement is given, defaults a remote host to verify-full, and prefers a unix socket with peer authentication.
controls.note: Not shown on the health page: SecurityBaseline::postgresTransportProblem() is not called for an already stored connection.

controls.how: HSTS and TLS rules are in the shipped nginx routes; the CSP-compatible headers are sent by the app; webhook destinations are https-only (WebhookDispatcher requireHttps) and plain http needs a per-destination, audit-logged opt-in.
controls.note: The nginx test covers private paths, not the HSTS value.

controls.how: Content-Security-Policy (nonce scripts), X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and Referrer-Policy are sent on every app page; Permissions-Policy comes from nginx; inline event handlers are banned by a guard test.
controls.note: Gaps: style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline'; the REST API sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (bearer tokens only, no cookies).

controls.how: Users and records can be exported and archived by an administrator; access is audit-logged.
controls.note: No self-service export or deletion of personal data and no test: partial by documentation only.

controls.how: deploy/backup.sh produces an openssl AES-256-CBC archive (600000 iterations, key file kept apart) that also holds the RMM PostgreSQL dump when that store is in use; the in-app backup includes the PostgreSQL dump as rmm-postgres.dump (a dump that is expected and fails fails the whole run). Every run records which stores it really contained (backup_runs.run_stores), and the compliance backup check reads encryption from the newest backup file's header (ArtifactCheckedBackupFactsProvider).
controls.note: Gap: the in-app zip is a plain archive (db.sql is not encrypted; only its manifest, which holds the settings key, is). The compliance check therefore reports it as not encrypted. Only the root pipeline (.enc) is fully encrypted. An unmerged branch (encrypt-admin-zip-backups) addresses this.

controls.how: Audit events are written for logins, MFA, permission and role changes, vault reveals, settings and backup events, and sealed in a hash chain that a nightly cron verifies. There is no setting that turns AuditService off.
controls.note: A database failure still propagates from AuditService to the caller by design.

controls.how: Audit retention is fed through SecurityBaseline::auditRetentionDays(), so the 90 day floor holds in the cron prune.
controls.note: The settings writes for password length, session timeout and MFA policy do not go through BaselineChanges::change() but they are audited by the settings handler.

controls.how: Audit logging cannot be switched off from the UI.
controls.note: Other locked-on baseline settings (tls_only, cookie_secure) are deployment configuration, not enforced by code.

controls.how: The installer asks for an existing database account and does not require a superuser; the RMM PostgreSQL store supports a unix socket with peer authentication and a dedicated role; a separate read-only reporting account is created from Administration > Reporting / Power BI with a generated password and grants on the reporting views only (tested: it cannot read base tables or write).
controls.note: The installer does not create the application's own database account; only the reporting account is created by the product.

controls.how: The root backup pipeline (deploy/backup.sh) always encrypts its archive. The in-app backup requires a passphrase but only encrypts the manifest that carries the settings key; the archive itself is a plain zip. There is no audit-logged override because encryption is not optional in the root pipeline.
controls.note: Gap against 'backups are encrypted by default' for the in-app zip. (tests/security_backup.php covers the passphrase rule, which is why this is not claimed as a proof.)

controls.how: Uploads are validated by type and size; there is no antivirus scan.
